Animated D3 bar-chart race

pv_race.Rd

The bar-chart race: at every time point the top_n entities appear as horizontal bars ranked by value, and the animation interpolates both values and ranks between consecutive time points, so bars grow and overtake each other smoothly while a large muted time label ticks along in the corner. Value labels ride the bar ends. Entities that rise into the ranking slide in from below the last visible row; entities that fall out slide down the same way. When the race finishes, a small circled-arrow control in the top-right corner replays it. Hovering a bar reads out the entity's exact value at the moment shown.

Usage

pv_race(
  data,
  time,
  id,
  value,
  top_n = 10,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  mode = "auto",
  duration = 500,
  source = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  elementId = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long form: one row per entity per time point (missing combinations mean the entity is absent then).

time

Name of the time column — numeric (e.g. a year) or Date. At least 2 distinct time points are required.

id

Name of the column identifying each racing entity.

value

Name of the numeric column the entities race on (non-negative; NA counts as absent).

top_n

How many ranked bars are visible at once (a whole number, at least 2; capped at the number of entities that ever qualify).

title, subtitle

Optional chart heading text.

mode

"auto" (default: follow the viewer's light/dark setting), "light", or "dark".

duration

Tempo control: each step between consecutive time points takes duration / 500 * 900 ms (never under 200 ms), so the default 500 gives roughly 900 ms per step. 0 skips the animation entirely and shows the final time point — no autoplay, but the replay control stays, and pressing it runs the race at the default tempo.

source

Optional source/credit line, shown small and grey at the bottom left — e.g. "Source: Bundesamt für Statistik".

width, height, elementId

Standard htmlwidgets sizing arguments.

Value

An htmlwidget.

Details

The entities in the race are everyone who makes the top_n at any time point, so late risers and early leaders all get their moment. Colours follow the final standings in palette-slot order; beyond the palette's 8 slots the colours repeat, faded toward the background.

Examples

pv_race(pv_city_population, time = "year", id = "city",
        value = "population", top_n = 12,
        title = "Swiss cities racing through a century",
        source = "Source: Bundesamt für Statistik")
